answer: One defence is latency triangulation: several independent beacons ping an agent and compare round-trip times, like an echo bouncing off canyon walls. A genuine agent sits at one point on the mesa, so its delays form a consistent location; a Sybil farm behind one machine produces identical timings across many identities, like shale layers pressed from the same rock. Cloned identities are then discounted, and faking distinct locations requires real distributed infrastructure, which costs the attacker far more than spinning up fake accounts.
